_comment: Documents whose measured claims about code are gated by
scripts/check-plan-doc-freshness.py.
EMPTY ON PURPOSE, 2026-08-06. The whole planning corpus was retired when the
owner replanned the product. There is no plan to enrol yet.
This is not a disabled gate. check-plan-doc-freshness.py treats the empty
state as a DEADLINE: it passes until PLAN_ENROLLMENT_DEADLINE and fails after,
so a replan that never produces a plan becomes a red build rather than a
silence. Clear it by enrolling the new plan here as 'anchored' AND naming it
in REQUIRED_ANCHORED -- not by moving the date.
status 'anchored': the document must carry a <!-- doc-freshness-anchor -->
block naming the commit it was measured at and the pathspecs it claims to
describe. The gate fails when commits touching those paths landed after the
anchor. Clearing the finding means re-measuring and advancing 'sha:'; editing
the document does not clear it.
status 'exempt': a dated, reasoned, EXPIRING escape hatch for a document that
is being migrated. An expired exemption is a failure. There is no permanent
exemption on purpose.
Any markdown file under the scan root (default: docs/) that carries an
anchor block is checked whether or not it is listed here; a missing scan
root scans as empty. Opting in costs one edit.

documents.reason: The replacement plan the 2026-08-06 interregnum was waiting for. Enrolled 2026-08-08, about five weeks before PLAN_ENROLLMENT_DEADLINE rather than left to expire: the gate names its own remedy, and a follow-up that waits on a deadline is a failure mode this repo already has a record of. The pathspecs are wide because the document's measured claims are wide -- which crates exist and how mature they are, that the graph-gate runs 'cargo check' and not 'cargo test' on the excluded crates, that two integration targets carry required-features, and what the backend workflow does. Each rots the moment its path moves, so each is named; a narrower anchor would read fresh while the claims went stale.
